key_insight: C2Seg aims to make medical image segmentation masks better match text descriptions, particularly when multiple sites or lesions are described.
clinical_relevance: Better text–mask agreement could support more faithful text-guided image analysis, but clinical benefit is not established by the abstract.
method: Cluster-aware contrastive pretraining uses soft text-similarity labels to reduce false-negative conflicts.
Bidirectional complementary attention strengthens spatial interaction between image and text features.
KAN-based attention gating enriches multimodal features while the language encoder remains frozen.
evidence_signal: The authors report improved text–mask consistency and segmentation accuracy on four public medical imaging datasets, without numerical results in the abstract.
watch_item: Performance on public datasets does not establish reliability across clinical settings; external validation remains important.
paper_title: Towards Text-Mask Consistency in Medical Image Segmentation
